abstract: Antimicrobial peptides were isolated from haemolymph of non-challenged and Escherichia coli-challenged fifth-instar Bombyx mori L. larvae by solvent extraction and reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography on a C18 column. Selected fractions were examined by liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry, and five peptide sequences with reported molecular masses of 1999.1731-3777.1000 Da were taken forward for computational analysis. Sequence composition, hydropathy, two-dimensional chemical representation, topology, and de novo three-dimensional models were evaluated using PEPTIDE 2.0, ProtScale, PepDraw, Protter, and PEP-FOLD. The candidates differed in length, charge-related residue content, and hydrophobicity. Leucine was abundant in all five sequences. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) validated peptide-induced bacterial morphological alterations, such as pore formation, cytoplasmic leakage, and cell lysis. Overall, B. mori-derived AMPs exhibited strong antimicrobial activity, either beating or rivalling broad-spectrum antibiotics, and provide good candidates for the development of alternative therapeutics against bacterial pathogens.

summary: Bombyx mori haemolymph peptides were purified, profiled with standard tools, and shown by SEM to disrupt bacterial membranes.
title: Purification, molecular characterization, and bioinformatics analysis of putative antimicrobial peptides isolated from the haemolymph of the mulberry silkworm, Bombyx mori.
